classification.difficultyReason: Construct a proof by combining Pythagoras’ theorem, difference-of-squares factorisation and logarithmic product and power laws.

content.prompt:
Consider a right-angled triangle with side lengths $a$, $b$ and $c$, with $c$ the hypotenuse.

Prove that $\log_{10}a=\frac12\log_{10}(c+b)+\frac12\log_{10}(c-b)$.

answer.short:
By Pythagoras’ theorem, $a^2=c^2-b^2=(c+b)(c-b)$.

Taking base-10 logarithms and applying the product and power laws gives $2\log_{10}a=\log_{10}(c+b)+\log_{10}(c-b)$. Divide by 2.
answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}a^2&=c^2-b^2\\a^2&=(c+b)(c-b).\end{align*}$$
Since the side lengths are positive and $c>b$, all logarithm arguments below are positive. Taking base-10 logarithms and using the product and power laws,
$$\begin{align*}\log_{10}(a^2)&=\log_{10}\bigl((c+b)(c-b)\bigr)\\2\log_{10}a&=\log_{10}(c+b)+\log_{10}(c-b)\\\log_{10}a&=\frac12\log_{10}(c+b)+\frac12\log_{10}(c-b).\end{align*}$$
